pr_title: Tensor Operation fixes when input is sliced (non-contiguous)
pr_body:
This pr Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/106280.

Basically when the input was being sliced, the Tensor operations weren't always respecting that. This caused extra data to be processed and in some cases changed the final output. Will be backported to 9.0.

issue_context.title: Incorrect result computed for tensor slices
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-numerics-tensors
See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
<!-- Policy app identification https://img.shields.io/static/v1?label=PullRequestIssueManagement. -->

This is because APIs like `TensorPrimitivesHelperTwoSpanInTOut` are currently just checking if the lengths are the same and the underlying storage size between them is the same: https://source.dot.net/#System.Numerics.Tensors/System/Numerics/Tensors/netcore/TensorExtensions.cs,949ec087cfc5ccfd

This is failing to account for there being "gaps" in the represented slice, which is the real factor for whether or not the linear buffer can be used directly and therefore avoid the inner loop.

review_comments:
For .NET 10 we should think about if we can use a bit or two to track that the span is contiguous/dense.

We should also ensure a tracking issue exists to ensure we can operate "row by row" and avoid allocating in the case that its not dense.
